geopolitics_summary: Von der Leyen signals energy ceasefire as Ukraine peace-talk metric; COP31 collapse raises climate policy uncertainty; EU nature-law relaxation debate signals pro-industry shift.

themes.headline: Von der Leyen: Energy ceasefire key signal of Putin peace intent
themes.why_it_matters: Renewed focus on Russia–Ukraine energy negotiations signals potential TTF volatility around peace-talk momentum. Any ceasefire agreement could ease winter gas supply fears and support Cal+1 curve flattening, but remains highly uncertain.

themes.headline: EU Parliament relaxes nature laws; accelerates permitting for industry
themes.why_it_matters: Faster environmental permitting reduces barriers to renewable and infrastructure projects; structural positive for near-term renewable capacity additions, putting downward pressure on power curve in 2027–28 horizon.

themes.headline: COP31 collapses; climate negotiations fail on fossil fuel commitments
themes.why_it_matters: Failed global climate accord weakens international consensus on emissions reduction, increasing regulatory risk for EU ETS carbon price; reduced near-term pressure on decarbonization targets supports coal/gas marginal economics and pressures EUA.

themes.headline: Big Oil and Trump officials delayed EU methane-reporting climate law
themes.why_it_matters: Delay in fossil-fuel methane disclosure rules reduces enforcement risk and cost for European gas producers; minor support for supply-side economics but immaterial to current TTF pricing given existing LNG glut.

themes.headline: U.S. natural gas storage ends injection season 2% above five-year average
themes.why_it_matters: Above-normal US nat-gas inventories (3,810 Bcf) reduce structural support for Henry Hub; likely increases LNG export availability into NW Europe spot market, strengthening TTF arbitrage supply and capping winter upside.

watchlist: Ukraine peace negotiations; track VdL signals on energy ceasefire mechanics and timing.
EU ETS auction outcomes; monitor carbon price reaction to COP31 collapse and green-permitting policy mix.
LNG export flows from US Gulf; above-avg storage may sustain higher TotIce/TTF arb into Dec–Jan.
EU budget negotiations; right-wing coalition could delay green-transition funding or renewable subsidy alignment.
